test_title: PYST 42: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 15 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: According to the Union Budget 2025-26, what increased credit allocation has been made for farmers, fishermen, and dairy farmers through the KCC (Kisan Credit Card)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹5 lakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Union Budget 2025-26**, the Government of India announced a significant enhancement in the credit limit available through the **Kisan Credit Card (KCC)** scheme to support the agricultural and allied sectors.
 
• The credit allocation for **farmers, fishermen, and dairy farmers** has been increased to **₹5 lakh** to ensure they have adequate liquidity for modernizing their operations and meeting working capital requirements. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• This move is specifically aimed at boosting the **Fisheries** (under PM Matsya Sampada Yojana) and **Animal Husbandry** sectors, which were previously integrated into the KCC fold to provide them with the same benefits as crop farmers.
 
• The **Union Finance Minister** emphasized that this increased limit will help in reducing the dependence of small-scale producers on informal credit sources and high-interest moneylenders.
 
• The budget for **2025-26** focuses on digital infrastructure in agriculture, and the **KCC** digital transformation is expected to make the disbursal of this **₹5 lakh** loan faster and more transparent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme:**

 
 
• The **KCC** scheme was introduced in **August 1998** based on the recommendations of the **R.V. Gupta Committee** to provide term loans and agricultural credit to farmers.
 
• It is implemented by **Commercial Banks**, **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)**, and **Cooperative Banks** under the overall guidance of **NABARD** and the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**.
 
 
 
• **Expansion of Scope:**
 
 
• In the **Budget 2018-19**, the government extended the **KCC** facility to **fisheries and animal husbandry** farmers to help them meet their working capital needs.
 
• The **Interest Subvention Scheme (ISS)** provides loans at a subsidized interest rate of **7% per annum**, with an additional **3% incentive** for prompt repayment, bringing the effective interest rate down to **4%** for many.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Allied Sectors:**
 
 
• The inclusion of **Dairy** and **Fisheries** ensures that these sectors, which contribute significantly to the **GVA (Gross Value Added)** of the Indian economy, receive formal financial support.
 
• For **fishermen**, the credit can be used for the purchase of **fishing nets, boats, and maintenance**, while for **dairy farmers**, it covers **cattle feed and veterinary expenses**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Institutional Credit Target:**

 
 
• For the financial year **2025-26**, the government has set a massive **Agricultural Credit Target** (often exceeding **₹20 lakh crore**) to ensure that the credit flow to the rural economy remains robust.
 
• The **PM-KISAN** database is frequently used to identify eligible farmers for **KCC**, ensuring **saturation** of the scheme across the country.
 
 
 
• **Key Features:**
 
 
• **Validity:** The **KCC** is usually valid for **5 years**, subject to annual reviews.
 
• **Insurance:** Beneficiaries are also covered under the **Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)** for accidental death or disability.
 
• **Collateral-free loans:** The limit for **collateral-free agricultural loans** was earlier raised to **₹1.6 lakh** to ease the burden on small and marginal farmers.
